segments.he: אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה וְתַחְבּוּלָה כִּי אִם לִצְעק אֶל בָּזֶה טוֹעִים רב בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד אוֹמֵר אִם הָיָה לוֹ פַּרְנָסָה הָיָה עוֹבֵד ה'. וְאִם כֵּן לְפִי דְּבָרָיו הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם בִּטְרוּנְיָא וַעֲלִילָה עִמּוֹ שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּעֲבד וְיַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל מֵחֲמַת דּחַק הַפַּרְנָסָה וְאִם כֵּן הֲרֵי הוּא מְהַרְהֵר אַחַר מִשְׁפָּטָיו שֶׁל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּאִלּוּ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם הוּא יִתְבָּרַךְ מְעַוֵּת הַמִּשְׁפָּט נֶגְדּוֹ. וְזֶה הַפְּגָם גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹתֵר כִּי כְּשֶׁמְּהַרְהֵר אַחַר מִשְׁפָּטָיו שֶׁל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ זֶהוּ עִקַּר בְּחִינַת פְּגַם הַמִּשְׁפָּט שֶׁמִּשָּׁם בָּאִים כָּל הַקִּלְקוּלִים הַנַּ"ל. עַל כֵּן צָרִיךְ כָּל הֶחָפֵץ בָּאֱמֶת לָחוּס עַל עַצְמוֹ שֶׁיִּזָּהֵר מְאד מִלּוֹמַר כַּדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה רַק יֵדַע וְיַאֲמִין שֶׁבְּחִירָתוֹ תְּלוּיָה דַּיְקָא בְּאפֶן זֶה שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְנַהֵג עִמּוֹ.
segments.en: And Esther is the aspect of the Kneses Yisrael — the aspect of the prayers of each and every person in Yisrael, praying in the force of the prolonging of their exile and trouble in body and soul. And she is called Esther after the name of concealment, in the aspect of "I will surely hide My face" [Devarim 31:18] — meaning that during the prolonging of exile it seems as if Hashem is hiding His face from us and as if the prayers are in vain, Heaven forbid. But the holy people of Yisrael — the aspect of Esther — strengthen themselves in prayer always, even in the force of the concealment within concealment. Even those of weakened strength among Yisrael who have no power to properly arrange their prayer — even when the wicked kingdom overpowers them in the aspect of "and Esther was taken to King Achashverosh" — even then they strengthen themselves in prayer always. As our Rabbis taught: when Esther entered into the house of Achashverosh and the Shechinah departed from her, she cried: "My G-d, my G-d, why have You forsaken me?" — a hint for every person in Yisrael: when one descends, Heaven forbid, to places where the Sitra Achra, the wicked kingdom, spreads and the holiness of the Shechinah departs — even then one must strengthen one's heart and cry out: "My G-d, my G-d, why have You forsaken me?" And all of Esther's strengthening to cry out always to Hashem was through Mordechai, who hinted this to her — for Mordechai, the aspect of the Tzaddik of the generation, is always engaged in teaching the entire Yisrael, the aspect of Esther, to strengthen themselves in prayer always, even during the prolonging of exile — for Hashem is still with them. And this is: "and he raised Hadassah, who is Esther, his uncle's daughter" [Esther 2:7] — for Esther is called Hadassah after the prayers engaged in always, which rise as a pleasant fragrance like myrtle. For even the prayers of those of weakened strength in Yisrael — which are in the aspect of Esther, the aspect of concealment — they too rise as a pleasant fragrance before Him through the Tzaddik of the generation, the aspect of Mordechai, to whom we bind our prayer, who raises even our prayer before Him as a fragrance of satisfaction. And this is: "she is Esther, daughter of his uncle" — in the aspect of barta d'malka [daughter of the King], called his uncle's daughter. And this is: "for she had no father and no mother" — father and mother are the aspect of the mochin: father in wisdom and mother in understanding. Since these weakened ones have no mochin, therefore the Tzaddik must raise and strengthen them each time — and this is the meaning of what our Rabbis taught: the word of Mordechai Esther did — as she had been in his upbringing with him — meaning that even while sitting in the lap of Achashverosh she would immerse and sit in the lap of Mordechai. For even when the force of the wicked kingdom overpowered her she strengthened herself each time and immersed and returned to Mordechai — that is, a G-d-fearing woman, the aspect of Esther, the aspect of the prayer of those of weakened strength, even when the impurity of the wicked kingdom overpowered her did not abandon her place and strengthened herself each time to purify and connect to the aspect of Mordechai — the Tzaddik of the generation — to fulfill the word of Mordechai who urges and strengthens her to multiply prayer always, whatever the situation.

segments.he: וְיַאֲמִין שֶׁהַכּל לְטוֹבָתוֹ וְיִהְיֶה רָגִיל לוֹמַר כָּל מַה דְּעָבֵד רַחֲמָנָא לְטָב עָבֵד וּבְוַדַּאי יֵשׁ דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁדַּיְקָא עַל יְדֵי זֶה הַדַּחֲקוּת וְהַיִּסּוּרִים וְהַבִּלְבּוּלִים יִתְקָרֵב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ. וְאִם קָשֶׁה לוֹ לְקַבֵּל וְלִסְבּל הַיִּסּוּרִים וְהַדַּחֲקוּת. יִצְעַק וְיִתְפַּלֵּל לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיּוֹשִׁיעוֹ וְיַעַזְרֵהוּ וּבָזֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ יִתְקָרֵב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיַעַבְדֵהוּ. כִּי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְאַוֶּה לִתְפִלָּתָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יִקְרָאֵנִי בְּיוֹם צָרָה אֲחַלֶּצְךָ וַתְּכַבְּדֵנִי כִּי אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה וְתַחְבּוּלָה נֶגֶד כָּל הַצָּרוֹת וְהַהַרְפַּתְקָאוֹת וְדַחֲקוּת וְטִרְדַּת הַפַּרְנָסָה הָעוֹבְרִים עַל כָּל הָאָדָם בְּכָל עֵת וָעֵת כִּי אִם לִצְעק וְלִזְעק וּלְהִתְחַנֵּן לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלִבְכּוֹת לְפָנָיו כְּתִינוֹק הַבּוֹכֶה לִפְנֵי אָבִיו שֶׁיְּמַלֵּא מַחְסוֹרוֹ.
segments.en: Every person must know this very well: according to the length of one's exile in desires and bad character traits — which is the primary exile — one must multiply prayer very greatly throughout all the days of one's vain life. And even when one sees that one prays greatly and is not answered, and the desires and confusions intensify each time further — even so, do not err that one's prayers and conversations are in vain, Heaven forbid. Rather, know and believe that no word is ever lost, and every prayer and conversation makes an impression — until the building that is needed is completed, then His compassion will be stirred and He will return to one and have mercy. And therefore one must strengthen oneself to multiply prayer and conversation always. But even so — when one has some salvation, do not err that through one's prayers and good deeds one accomplished this. Rather know that everything is in His kindness. And even though we know that we are unable to effect the complete salvation through our prayers, even so we must do our part and multiply prayer as much as we can — and then His compassion will be stirred and He will do His part in His kindness for His own sake and save us speedily.

segments.he: וּכְשֶׁיֵּלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה יַרְוִיחַ תָּמִיד הַרְבֵּה רֶוַח הָאֲמִתִּי וְהַנִּצְחִי כִּי עַל פִּי רב יִפְעל בְּבַקָּשָׁתוֹ הַרְבֵּה כִּי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלַּת כָּל פֶּה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב קָרוֹב ה' לְכָל קרְאָיו וְכוּ' וַאֲפִלּוּ אִם לִפְעָמִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לא יִתְקַבֵּל תְּפִלָּתוֹ כִּי זמנין דשמע זימנין דְּלָא שמע. עַל כָּל פָּנִים הִרְוִיחַ שֶׁקֵּרֵב עַצְמוֹ לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה. כִּי אֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר שֶׁיְּקָרֵב וִידַבֵּק אֶת הָאָדָם לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁהִיא עִקַּר הִתְחַבְּרוּת וּדְבֵקוּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא סִימָן פ"ד דַּע שֶׁעִקַּר הִתְחַבְּרוּת וְכוּ'):
segments.en: And this too is included in what is written in the Torah teaching above: that in prayer one must aim at the hair's breadth and not miss — meaning not to veer right or left. That is, not to err, Heaven forbid, that prayers are in vain because one has been crying for so long without being saved — which is the aspect of veering to the left, making His attribute of mercy appear as if He is cruel, Heaven forbid, as if Hashem does not hear the prayer of Yisrael. And similarly, do not err to say: since we cannot effect salvation through our prayers but only through His kindness — why should we multiply prayer at all? Let us rely on His kindness alone. For this too is a great error — the aspect of veering to the right improperly, relying only on His kindness. For in truth both together are good: one must multiply prayer very greatly always, and know the truth that we are not worthy to effect anything through our prayers except through His kindness. And even so we must do our part and multiply prayer greatly always — and Hashem will do His part and draw upon us His kindness for His own sake and save us speedily.

segments.he: אֲבָל זֶה שֶׁאוֹמֵר הָאָדָם אִם הָיָה כָּךְ הָיִיתִי עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה וְכוּ' אֵין זֶה עֵצָה כְּלָל וְהוּא פּוֹגֵם בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה בְּחִינַת פְּגַם הַמִּשְׁפָּט כַּנַּ"ל. כִּי כָּל אֶחָד צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא שָׁם אֶת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם מִשָּׁם אֶת ה' אֱלקֶיךָ וּמָצָאתָ וְכוּ' מִשָּׁם דַּיְקָא מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה שָׁם מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר עָלֶיךָ וְכַמּוּבָא בְּשֵׁם הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זַ"ל. (שָׁם הֲלָכָה ו אוֹת יא):
segments.en: This is the aspect of the great and immense value of making prayers from Torah teachings — for all the Torah one studies enters into the prayer and is renewed there, and they strengthen each other, as above. And this applies even when the Torah one studies does not have an obvious connection to the prayer — for example, studying laws of monetary matters and then praying about the observance of Shabbos and the like. But certainly it is an even greater and mightier value when one merits to make a prayer from the very Torah one is engaged in — for then Torah and prayer are in far more complete unity, and they strengthen each other and illuminate each other more and more. And therefore this matter of making prayers from Torah teachings is exceedingly, exceedingly precious — and from this great delights are made above that have no equal, as explained in his holy words of blessed memory. For through this one unifies Torah and prayer in a wondrous unification until they become complete unity — and they strengthen each other greatly.

aligned_segments.en: And even when one sees that one prays greatly and is not answered, and the desires and confusions intensify each time further — even so, do not err that one's prayers and conversations are in vain, Heaven forbid. Rather, know and believe that no word is ever lost, and every prayer and conversation makes an impression — until the building that is needed is completed, then His compassion will be stirred and He will return to one and have mercy.

aligned_segments.he: יִצְעַק וְיִתְפַּלֵּל לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיּוֹשִׁיעוֹ וְיַעַזְרֵהוּ וּבָזֶה בְּעַצְמוֹ יִתְקָרֵב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְיַעַבְדֵהוּ.
aligned_segments.en: And therefore one must strengthen oneself to multiply prayer and conversation always. But even so — when one has some salvation, do not err that through one's prayers and good deeds one accomplished this.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מִתְאַוֶּה לִתְפִלָּתָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב יִקְרָאֵנִי בְּיוֹם צָרָה אֲחַלֶּצְךָ וַתְּכַבְּדֵנִי כִּי אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה וְתַחְבּוּלָה נֶגֶד כָּל הַצָּרוֹת וְהַהַרְפַּתְקָאוֹת וְדַחֲקוּת וְטִרְדַּת הַפַּרְנָסָה הָעוֹבְרִים עַל כָּל הָאָדָם בְּכָל עֵת וָעֵת כִּי אִם לִצְעק וְלִזְעק וּלְהִתְחַנֵּן לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלִבְכּוֹת לְפָנָיו כְּתִינוֹק הַבּוֹכֶה לִפְנֵי אָבִיו שֶׁיְּמַלֵּא מַחְסוֹרוֹ.
aligned_segments.en: Rather know that everything is in His kindness. And even though we know that we are unable to effect the complete salvation through our prayers, even so we must do our part and multiply prayer as much as we can — and then His compassion will be stirred and He will do His part in His kindness for His own sake and save us speedily.

aligned_segments.he: וּכְשֶׁיֵּלֵךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ זֶה יַרְוִיחַ תָּמִיד הַרְבֵּה רֶוַח הָאֲמִתִּי וְהַנִּצְחִי כִּי עַל פִּי רב יִפְעל בְּבַקָּשָׁתוֹ הַרְבֵּה כִּי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹמֵעַ תְּפִלַּת כָּל פֶּה וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב קָרוֹב ה' לְכָל קרְאָיו וְכוּ' וַאֲפִלּוּ אִם לִפְעָמִים חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לא יִתְקַבֵּל תְּפִלָּתוֹ כִּי זמנין דשמע זימנין דְּלָא שמע.
aligned_segments.en: And this too is included in what is written in the Torah teaching above: that in prayer one must aim at the hair's breadth and not miss — meaning not to veer right or left. That is, not to err, Heaven forbid, that prayers are in vain because one has been crying for so long without being saved — which is the aspect of veering to the left, making His attribute of mercy appear as if He is cruel, Heaven forbid, as if Hashem does not hear the prayer of Yisrael.

aligned_segments.he: עַל כָּל פָּנִים הִרְוִיחַ שֶׁקֵּרֵב עַצְמוֹ לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי זֶה.
aligned_segments.en: And similarly, do not err to say: since we cannot effect salvation through our prayers but only through His kindness — why should we multiply prayer at all? Let us rely on His kindness alone.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי אֵין שׁוּם דָּבָר שֶׁיְּקָרֵב וִידַבֵּק אֶת הָאָדָם לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ הַתְּפִלָּה שֶׁהִיא עִקַּר הִתְחַבְּרוּת וּדְבֵקוּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּלִקּוּטֵי תִּנְיָנָא סִימָן פ"ד דַּע שֶׁעִקַּר הִתְחַבְּרוּת וְכוּ'):
aligned_segments.en: For this too is a great error — the aspect of veering to the right improperly, relying only on His kindness. For in truth both together are good: one must multiply prayer very greatly always, and know the truth that we are not worthy to effect anything through our prayers except through His kindness. And even so we must do our part and multiply prayer greatly always — and Hashem will do His part and draw upon us His kindness for His own sake and save us speedily.

aligned_segments.he: אֲבָל זֶה שֶׁאוֹמֵר הָאָדָם אִם הָיָה כָּךְ הָיִיתִי עוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה וְכוּ' אֵין זֶה עֵצָה כְּלָל וְהוּא פּוֹגֵם בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה בְּחִינַת פְּגַם הַמִּשְׁפָּט כַּנַּ"ל.
aligned_segments.en: This is the aspect of the great and immense value of making prayers from Torah teachings — for all the Torah one studies enters into the prayer and is renewed there, and they strengthen each other, as above. And this applies even when the Torah one studies does not have an obvious connection to the prayer — for example, studying laws of monetary matters and then praying about the observance of Shabbos and the like.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי כָּל אֶחָד צָרִיךְ לְבַקֵּשׁ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁהוּא שָׁם אֶת ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם מִשָּׁם אֶת ה' אֱלקֶיךָ וּמָצָאתָ וְכוּ' מִשָּׁם דַּיְקָא מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה שָׁם מִכָּל מַה שֶּׁעוֹבֵר עָלֶיךָ וְכַמּוּבָא בְּשֵׁם הַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זַ"ל. (שָׁם הֲלָכָה ו אוֹת יא):
aligned_segments.en: But certainly it is an even greater and mightier value when one merits to make a prayer from the very Torah one is engaged in — for then Torah and prayer are in far more complete unity, and they strengthen each other and illuminate each other more and more. And therefore this matter of making prayers from Torah teachings is exceedingly, exceedingly precious — and from this great delights are made above that have no equal, as explained in his holy words of blessed memory. For through this one unifies Torah and prayer in a wondrous unification until they become complete unity — and they strengthen each other greatly.
